summary:
MARS COMMAND: SURVIVE & LEARN

MARS COMMAND: Survive & Learn is an educational adventure game that puts players in the shoes of an astronaut trying to survive on Mars.

We developed an interactive Mars research base where players can explore, drive a rover, grow food in a greenhouse, collect rock samples, and solve engineering problems. Throughout the game, players face challenges involving oxygen, energy, water, radiation, atmospheric pressure, and food supplies.

Our game addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by helping young people understand the science and engineering behind living on another planet. Instead of just reading about these challenges, players experience them firsthand. They repair equipment, manage limited resources, and see how their decisions affect the entire base.

We also connect the gameplay to real NASA missions, such as Apollo 13, Opportunity, and MOXIE, showing how space exploration has inspired solutions to difficult problems.

We created MARS COMMAND because we believe science is easier to understand when you can experiment, make mistakes, and learn by doing. Our goal is to make space education more engaging, accessible, and enjoyable for the next generation of explorers.
details:
We started MARS COMMAND with a simple question: What would happen if we were on Mars and something went wrong with our base?

We wanted to create a game where students could experience these situations instead of just reading about them.

We developed MARS COMMAND: Survive & Learn using Godot 4 and GDScript. It is a 2.5D adventure game where players control an astronaut living at a small research base on Mars.

Players can explore the base, interact with equipment, investigate technical problems, and make decisions to keep the base running. The game introduces challenges involving electricity, oxygen, water, food, radiation, and atmospheric pressure.

For example, when a dust storm reduces solar power, players must investigate what happened and figure out how to protect the base's essential systems.

We also wanted to connect the game to real space exploration. We researched NASA missions such as Apollo 13, Opportunity, and MOXIE to help explain the science behind the challenges.

What makes our project different is that we want players to learn through their own decisions. They can try different solutions, make mistakes, and understand why certain choices work better than others.

Our goal is to make space science more interesting and easier to understand for students who might one day become scientists, engineers, or astronauts.
